introduction: On this Sunday, Malachi rebukes priests who have turned from God's way and shown partiality. In the Gospel, Jesus warns against religious leaders who say but do not do, and who seek honor and titles; he says the greatest among us must be our servant. Paul recalls how he cared for the Thessalonians as gently as a nursing mother. Let us serve with humility and integrity.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, God is our one Father, and we are all brothers and sisters. Let us bring him our prayers.
intentions: For the Pope, bishops, priests and all who lead in the Church: that they may practice what they preach and serve with humility. Let us pray to the Lord.
For teachers and all who guide others: that they may care for those entrusted to them as Paul cared for the Thessalonians. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who carry heavy burdens laid on them by others: that they may find help and relief. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who seek honor and recognition: that they may discover the greatness of serving. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may humble ourselves, so that God may exalt us. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Lord God, you are our one Father and Christ is our one teacher. Make us humble servants of one another, faithful in word and deed. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: The greatest among you
reflection.body:
Through the prophet Malachi, God speaks sternly to the priests of his time. They have "turned away from the path" and "caused many to stumble." They have shown favoritism instead of justice. Malachi reminds them of a basic truth: "Don't we all have one father? Hasn't one God created us?" Those who lead God's people are called to faithfulness and fairness.

In the Gospel, Jesus speaks to the crowds and to his disciples about the scribes and Pharisees. He does not reject their teaching: "All things therefore whatever they tell you to observe, observe and do." But he warns against their example: "don't do their works; for they say, and don't do." They "bind heavy burdens" on others but will not lift a finger to help. They do their good works "to be seen by men," and love the places of honor.

Jesus is speaking about a temptation that faces every religious person, and especially those who lead: to say one thing and do another, to use religion for status. His warning applies to the Church in every age.

Then he gives the alternative: "one is your teacher, the Christ, and all of you are brothers." And: "he who is greatest among you will be your servant. Whoever exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted."

Paul offers a beautiful picture of a leader who serves. He reminds the Thessalonians how he behaved among them: "we were gentle among you, like a nursing mother cherishes her own children." He shared with them "not the Good News of God only, but also our own souls."

The psalm expresses the humble heart: "LORD, my heart isn't arrogant, nor my eyes lofty." This week, pray for your priests and leaders. And look at your own life: do you practice what you say you believe? Choose one way to serve without being seen.
